newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banking shares hit by renewed selling.
newsitem.headline: Japan banking shares hit by renewed selling.

text.p: Japanese banking shares were battered by a renewed wave of selling on Tuesday morning, after a round of buying back the previous day, amid lingering worries over the sectors' bad debts, brokers said.
Sakura Bank Ltd shares were down 47 yen at 693 yen as of 0104 GMT. Volume was 2.49 million shares, making it the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Nippon Credit Bank shares shed 12 yen to stand at 247 yen. The volume of 2.46 million shares was the second heaviest traded volume.
Fuji Bank Ltd shed 90 yen to 1,460 yen, the Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd 8315 T lost 70 to 1,900 and Sumitomo Bank Ltd 8318 T lost 80 to 1,450.
"There was demand for buying back yesterday, but we couldn't see fresh buying. Bank shares will likely stay under selling pressures for a while," said a broker at a major securities house.
